sentences.text:
Ananda H.M. vs Radha M. on 18 September, 2023
Bench: Abhay S. Oka, Pankaj Mithal
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Criminal Appeal No. Of 2023
 (Arising Out Of S.L.P. (Criminal) No.7735 Of 2021)
 Ananda H.M. 
 Versus
 Radha M. & Anr. 
 O R D E R
Heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties.
Leave granted.
The respondent no.1 has been duly served.
However, none appears for her.
The High Court granted bail to the appellant by the order d
ated 30th March, 2021

. The offence alleged was under Sections 376, 406, 313, 354, 417, 504, 506 and 509 of the Indian Penal Code,
1860.
The High Court proceeded on the footing that the relationship was consensual.
By the impugned order dated 7th September, 2021, bail granted to the appellant has been cancelled on the ground of certain postings made by the appellant on the social media.
On 8th October, 2021, this Court while issuing notice, stayed the operation of the impugned order cancelling the bail.
After having heard the learned counsel appearing for the State, we find that there is no grievance made about any misuse of the liberty granted to him by the appellant after 8 th October, 2021.
Therefore, a case is made out to set aside the impugned order.
Accordingly, the impugned order dated 7th September, 2021, is set aside and the order dated 30th March, 2021, by which the bail was granted to the appellant, is restored.
We, however, make it clear that the appellant shall scrupulously observe and comply with the conditions on which the bail was granted to him.
In the case of default, it will always be open for the respondents to apply for cancellation of bail.
The Appeal is accordingly allowed.
